  • Functional: changes to actions, setup, outcomes, required data, scenario boundaries or coverage require admitted evidence under the common source rules. A clear, explicit user requirement is evidence; ask only if the intended behaviour is ambiguous or conflicts with another requirement.
  • Never infer correctness from the existing feature or Python alone. Do not weaken assertions, delete failing cases, replace data or add unsupported paths merely to make a correction look complete.

docs.title: 3. Reconcile registered UC output
docs.text:
For a registered feature, follow UC resumption and invalidation before overwriting it. Confirm continuity, preserve manual changes and respect producer ownership. The analyst may apply the owning skill's procedure directly; this is not delegation to another analyst.

  • A feature-only correction requires reconciling that feature and the final report through uc-to-feature, updating real revisions, mapping, coverage, checks and the registry. Unchanged context/data need not be retrieved again.
  • A change to requirements, oracle or data constraints returns first to context; a data-only change returns to data. Apply the existing downstream invalidation graph; never rewrite another stage's report as a shortcut.
  • If prerequisites or permissions prevent reconciliation, do not overwrite a registered feature blindly. Report the blocker. If explicitly authorized edits are saved before reconciliation can finish, mark the feature and final report stale in the registry, move the run to in_progress, and report the incomplete reconciliation. Never leave the old ready/complete claim in effect.
  • If the registry cannot be updated, report the actual failure and which files were saved; treat the result as blocked, not a completed/current UC stage.

docs.title: 4. Apply and check
docs.text:
• Make only the scoped edits at the agreed paths, integrating current contents. Do not create replacement feature files or split/rename files unless the request or a subsequent human decision authorizes those output paths.
  • Check language, keyword roles, outline parameters/tables, tags, independence, data placeholders, source-supported outcomes and preservation of intended coverage. Reconcile TODO comments when the associated input is resolved.
  • For outline normalization, preserve distinct rows/Examples tags and source coverage; consider table/docstring placeholders and changed binding text. Preserve stable identifiers on insertions/reordering. Renumbering/splitting needs authorized paths, an old/new identity mapping and workflow reconciliation.
  • Distinguish intentional null cells from missing data and empty strings. Hand off the mandatory empty-cell-to-None conversion for new/changed bindings; feature syntax alone does not verify conversion.
  • The analyst performs static inspection with read tools, not parser commands, tests, Git commands or environment queries. The only terminal exception remains behave --lang-help <language code>. Label externally supplied validation results as external; do not claim a parser/test was run by the analyst.
  • Surface failed writes or partial completion explicitly. Do not report changes that exist only as proposals in chat as saved files.

docs.title: 5. Return the result
docs.text: Use the activity result contract: changed paths, corrections and their evidence, checks actually performed, unresolved issues, per-feature readiness and Python implementation impact. Show old/new step wording or parameter changes where bindings may be affected. Explain changed tags/outline expansion when test selection or generated cases may change. Do not edit the Python or delegate implementation; the orchestrator decides whether the development gate is met.

docs.title: QA closure workflow (ADR-08 through ADR-13)
docs.text:
QA-closer prepares documentation and performs only authorized publication actions. It does not run tests, fix code/features, choose a new branch, or capture ACE traces. Read the complete workflow before closure; stop if required inputs cannot be read.

For a documentation-only assignment, use actual scoped inputs and perform only the requested README/ignore maintenance; runtime verification, a commit message and publication decisions are not prerequisites to saving authorized documentation. Use not-applicable where appropriate. This exception never authorizes Git publication or a standalone success report; publication still requires all applicable evidence/action gates below.

docs.title: Closure input contract (ADR-08)
docs.text:
The orchestrator supplies the following facts, using explicit unknown or not-applicable for missing evidence rather than invented success:

Input Required content Identity and scope Expected work branch; Jira key if known; current ACE request ID; UC identity if applicable; exact intended files and work type Verification Runner's exact command, suite/environment, time, branch/revision and relevant working-tree contents verified, exit status, passed/failed/error/skipped/undefined counts, exclusions and flaky findings Evidence Actual output/artifact/log paths or accessible references; what was not checked; whether verification covers all requested changes Documentation README assessment and its covered contents/scope, if already performed Publication plan Independent commit, push and create_pr decisions (true, false or unresolved), exact commit message, remote/head/base choices and PR inputs where applicable Prior closure state README assessment, error report, commit hash, push result and PR URL already produced, including errors or partial completion

A larger test count or a previously failing test is not required for a legitimate update/refactor. Passing applicable checks of the intended changes is the normal publication gate. The runner supplies evidence, not just "all green".

Before publication, compare evidence against the actual relevant current contents, including staged/unstaged inputs, configuration and dependencies. A matching HEAD alone does not establish freshness for uncommitted changes. Missing/unreadable artifacts, unexplained exclusions, zero executed tests, relevant undefined/skipped cases or unresolved flaky findings do not count as blanket success. Return gaps to the orchestrator for the runner or a scoped human decision; do not rerun tests or waive failures yourself. Do not demand the full repository suite when targeted verification adequately covers the authorized change.

Reader-only documentation and ignore updates do not automatically invalidate test results; changes to execution inputs or executable code/configuration do. If relevant contents changed after verification, stop publication and request fresh evidence. Never relabel an unverified result as passed.

docs.title: Actions and approval gates (ADR-09 and ADR-10)
docs.text:
1. Check terminal type and repository state from the root using read-only Git commands. Confirm the current branch is the expected work branch. Detached HEAD, main, the repository default branch, or any unexpected branch blocks Git publication. Report it; do not checkout, switch, create a branch or repair routing inside QA-closer.
  2. Confirm exact intended files and preserve pre-existing staging/edits. Add only relevant README/ignore outputs explicitly covered by closure. Unrelated staged content blocks a commit until its scope is resolved; do not include it or unstage it silently. Do not stage local reports or ignored files forcibly.
  3. Resolve each action independently through the dedicated question tool only when needed. Reuse clear user authorizations; explicit refusal takes precedence.
Decision Meaning commit: true Create a scoped commit after the evidence gate, using the exact orchestrator message push: true Publish the authorized commits to the confirmed destination, after the evidence gate create_pr: true Open/reuse the authorized PR after the evidence gate and required publication Any explicit false Skip that action; do not ask again to override a refusal Unresolved decision Ask before that action; test success does not supply consent

A PR request can use an already published branch without a new commit or push. If a PR needs an unpublished commit but push is forbidden, report the dependency and stop that action; do not override the refusal. create_pr: false does not cancel an independently authorized commit/push. A no-push/commit-only restriction must be passed explicitly to the commit skill rather than relying on its default.

  1. Before a push, inspect outgoing commits as well as the current index: existing commits can contain unrelated or unverified work. If their authorization or verified scope is unclear, stop and resolve it. Recheck branch, destination, relevant contents and approval before each publication action, including resume.
  2. Use ppa-commit as the Git procedure source, passing the exact file scope, message and push restriction. Preserve the subject/body and apply its required trailer policy. A message conflict is a blocker, not permission to rewrite the orchestrator message. For an authorized push-only action or retry of an existing commit, use only the skill's push procedure; never invoke its commit/staging steps again.
  3. Use ppa-pr only when authorized. Preserve reviewers, release labels, explicit source/target routing and PR template rules. PR-body completion is not a standalone error report. Reuse existing PRs rather than creating duplicates; do not silently edit an existing PR without permission.

No merge, force push, amend, history rewriting, hook bypass, staging-all shortcut, secret publication or generated-output inclusion is authorized by closure.

docs.title: Documentation and ignore maintenance (ADR-11)
docs.text:
Apply ppa-readme once for the current coherent change set, or reuse an assessment that actually covers its current contents. A new suite may need usage/location documentation; a fix may need a targeted correction or no README change. Correct obsolete material instead of appending duplicate suite sections. Report no-update-needed when appropriate.

Inspect existing ignore rules only for new local/generated outputs from this work. Add a narrowly scoped rule only if needed; preserve existing rules and tracked files. Do not create or edit .gitignore merely because closure ran. Local ignored reports remain local; publication requires a separate authorized destination, not an automatic ignore exception.

docs.title: Error-only Markdown reporting (ADR-12)
docs.text:
Create or update a standalone closure report only for work on test suites with unresolved errors in the relevant evidence, including unresolved intermittent failures explicitly reported by the runner. Successful work, non-suite repository maintenance, a missing count increase, or a Git/PR/tool failure alone does not generate a suite report. Earlier failures resolved by current verified results do not require a new error report.

  • Normal publication requires successful verification. With unresolved suite errors, the orchestrator may request report-only closure: no commit, push or PR through this path. A possible partial/failing-work publication requires a separate explicit decision outside successful closure, not a warning bypass.
  • First reuse the runner's relevant Markdown failure report when it already documents the same evidence. Do not generate a duplicate for the same failure. If a report is missing/incomplete, write or extend an agreed .md path under reports/, preserving existing findings and recording the evidence used.
  • Write in Italian: concise summary and counts, affected tests/files, actual errors and limited traceback evidence, established/suspected cause distinguished, attempts, remaining blockers and next steps. Do not invent execution or counts. Unknown values remain unknown; unavailable evidence is an explicit limitation.
  • No HTML/Allure generation or serving, Confluence templates/API, external publication, or template lookup for a standalone report. The GitHub PR template remains mandatory when creating a PR through ppa-pr.
  • Use only actual runner artifacts; do not run tests to reconstruct a report. Avoid secrets and personal data. A failed report write is an explicit partial failure, not a saved report. Final chat status and ACE trace elements remain required even when no standalone report is applicable.

docs.title: ACE boundary and recovery (ADR-13)
docs.text:
The analyst/engineer/runner/closer return trace elements; the orchestrator owns capture and project privacy finalization. Do not create or edit ACE files here. ACE files are excluded from closure scope by default. Include only explicitly authorized trace files with actual evidence of successful privacy finalization for those contents; a filename or a human statement alone is not proof of a successful sanitization command. Raw or uncertain trace contents must not be staged, committed or published.

The closer's own trace is captured after its result by the orchestrator. It need not be in the commit it describes. There is no recursive commit to include that trace and no second automatic publication after finalization.

Return actual state before stopping. On resumption, verify recorded state using read-only Git/gh checks; do not infer success from an earlier attempted command.

Last verified state Resume behavior No commit created Reconcile partial documentation/report writes, current scope, evidence and approval before retrying Commit created, push failed or not attempted Preserve the hash; retry only the authorized push, not a new commit Push verified, PR failed or not attempted Recheck authorization and existing PR, then perform only the needed PR step PR verified Return its actual metadata/URL; do not duplicate it Prior state cannot be established Report the uncertainty and ask before any potentially duplicate write

The same approved actions may be retried only within unchanged scope/destination; new edits, commits, destinations or a later refusal require reassessment. Never amend to hide a failed step. New uncommitted work is not part of a prior commit and does not justify repeating the old closure blindly.

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
Return a concise result to the orchestrator, not only the commit/PR skill's individual output:

  • Closure mode and result: completed, report-only, partial or blocked; verified evidence scope and unresolved issues.
  • README assessment/changed sections; ignore changes or why unnecessary.
  • Error report path actually saved/reused, or not-applicable; not a success report.
  • Commit message/hash or explicit not-created/skipped; push destination/result and PR URL/result, with failed, skipped and existing states distinguished.
  • Next safe action for recovery, if any.
  • Actual actions, checks, lesson IDs and friction for the current ACE request.

Never claim an artifact, published branch, completed PR or passed test without its corresponding evidence.

docs.title: QA closure contract validation
docs.text:
The closure workflow and ppa-readme are checked by the existing QA contract tests:

.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest tests\unit\qa_workflow\test_uc_workflow_contract.py -q

These are development-time contract checks, not permissions for QA-closer to run tests. They check asset clauses, tables, links and metadata, not a simulated agent or real publication. A behavioural trial needs actual user-authorized inputs and observed tool results. The following table records expected outcomes, not evidence that these scenarios have been executed.

Case Input or state Expected result C-01 Passing targeted verification of a legitimate update without increased test count Accept applicable evidence; no artificial improvement or full-suite requirement C-02 Executable/configuration changes after the reported run Stop publication and return to orchestrator for fresh evidence; no closer test rerun C-03 Unexpected branch, main/default branch or detached HEAD No publication or branch repair; explain the mismatch C-04 Unrelated staged files or outgoing commits Stop the affected publication until scope is resolved; preserve unrelated work C-05 Green tests with create_pr false No PR; independently authorized commit/push remain possible C-06 Commit-only request Pass no-push restriction to ppa-commit; no implicit PR C-07 PR requested, unpublished commits, push forbidden Report dependency; never override refusal C-08 Existing published branch and authorized PR, no new commit/push Use existing branch and existing-PR checks without an empty commit C-09 Current README assessment covers unchanged relevant contents Reuse it; no duplicate append, cosmetic edit or recursive assessment C-10 Restricted role discovers a README correction Return required change for an authorized writer; do not bypass permissions C-11 Successful suite work or non-suite maintenance No standalone closure report or HTML generation C-12 Unresolved suite errors with a runner Markdown report Reuse report in report-only mode; no commit/push/PR C-13 Report needed but missing evidence or write failure Mark unknowns/failure explicitly; no invented counts or saved-report claim C-14 Commit created, push failed Verify existing hash and retry only authorized push C-15 Push verified, PR failed or already exists Recheck authorization/existing PR and resume only needed PR action C-16 Closer returns before its ACE trace exists Orchestrator captures/finalizes later; no raw trace staging or recursive commit

When trying these with an agent, record input scope, authorizations, actual evidence, partial results and the observed next action. Passing static assertions does not prove that a live agent or Git operation followed this procedure.

docs.title: QA engineer activity and implementation workflow
docs.text: This is the mandatory entry for direct user requests, orchestrator assignments and runner fixes. It implements ADR-14 through ADR-19. Branch routing remains the orchestrator's responsibility; this workflow authorizes no Git operations.

docs.title: Activity routing (ADR-14)
docs.text:
Activity Behavior Allowed output Review Apply review-behave-steps directly when already QA-engineer; never self-delegate Findings in chat and an explicitly requested Markdown report at an agreed path; no code or feature writes Implement or extend Require the implementation input contract, reuse existing bindings, implement authorized behaviour Scoped step/binding and necessary suite-hook edits Fix or refactor Establish the defect or preservation goal and authorized files before editing Scoped corrections preserving unrelated behaviour and coverage

Use explicit intent without redundant permission questions. Ask if the activity, files, expected behaviour or scope is ambiguous. Supplied files alone do not authorize editing. A review never becomes a fix without an explicit activity change. Explanation-only requests remain in chat.

Review can examine incomplete code or draft features without passing the implementation readiness gate. Findings must distinguish proven code defects, missing functional evidence and suggestions. No corrected copies of code may be created during review. Report permission is not permission to write UCs, skills, instructions, execution config, ACE files or implementation code.

docs.title: Input and functional boundary (ADR-15)
docs.text:
For implementation receive the current feature paths/contents, analyst explanation, per-feature readiness, suite type/framework, target files, approved scope and ownership. Check these even when invoked directly, not only through an orchestrator. For UC features, consume current registry/report readiness; do not reconstruct requirements from Python or silently use stale/draft artifacts.

Stop affected implementation on unresolved functional requirements, oracles, required setup/data, TODO placeholders or contradictory inputs. Ask the user or return the gap to the orchestrator for QA-analyst; do not edit the feature, choose an expected result, substitute plausible data, or turn placeholders into runtime defaults. A ready subset requires explicit scope authorization.

For new/changed bindings follow the empty-Examples-cell contract: accept raw empty outline text and interpret it as Python None before typed conversion or payload construction. Preserve JSON null rather than omitting it or stringifying it. Receive the analyst's affected parameters/rows and agreed missing/empty/null distinctions; unresolved representation returns to the analyst. Propose checks of matcher acceptance, actual decoding and serialization, not only parser syntax. No global parser patch or bulk migration of legacy suites.

For a fix, obtain the failing scenario, actual error/traceback when available, expected behaviour and target scope. A clearly described static defect does not require fabricating a failed run. For a refactor, identify behaviour and public bindings to preserve. Existing-test maintenance does not require a new UC run, but unresolved requirements remain blockers. Never use pass, unconditional success, skipped assertions, broad exception suppression, weakened checks or disabled scenarios as a completion shortcut.

docs.title: Suite context and reuse (ADR-16)
docs.text:
Read the Python instructions and, for step/binding/hook work, the Behave instructions and profile. Confirm the actual framework: Behave bindings, pytest-bdd fixtures and Playwright automation are not interchangeable. Playwright can be used inside Behave without changing its binding framework.

For an existing suite, use its own loading rules, hooks, matcher, context lifecycle and conventions; do not require a second blueprint choice merely because none was passed. For a new suite, find compatible technical references and ask only if the choice or missing conventions materially affects implementation. Blueprints supply technical patterns, not product requirements or expected values. Do not copy another suite's environment assumptions or data.

Inspect the shared utility documentation listed in the profile and applicable module APIs before adding logic. Resolve local utility paths with the actual <test-type> and <suite>; never place API/E2E helpers under integration by default. Inspect the full relevant loaded step scope for reusable definitions and matcher collisions, not only the feature's proposed new file. Apply Behave coding conventions (ADR-38 through ADR-43): organization follows cohesive suite responsibilities, binding checks include kind/matcher/conversions, and context/reset/cleanup respect actual lifecycle scopes. Profile paths guide reuse/new helpers, not automatic legacy migrations. Preserve full logical assertions and structured input semantics, with bounded observation waits and safe diagnostics. These conventions do not expand writing or execution permissions.

docs.title: File and utility ownership (ADR-17)
docs.text:
QA-engineer owns authorized step definitions, bindings, assertions and necessary suite wiring in environment.py or equivalent hooks. Hook edits must be within scope and respect existing cleanup/context lifecycle; new targets require scope confirmation. Do not turn hooks or step files into a reusable utility layer.

Python-utility-engineer owns new reusable helpers and changes to existing utility modules, both suite-local and shared src/utility. Call existing documented APIs directly when sufficient. Delegate only a concrete missing utility change, with:

  • Exact owned paths and requested API/signature.
  • Supported behaviour, inputs, expected outputs/errors and compatibility needs.
  • Existing helpers considered and why they do not suffice.
  • Relevant unit-test cases and integration expectations.

The specialist returns API, files, compatibility impact, tests written and checks actually performed. Integrate its result only after reading the changed API. Use its utility workflow contract: include relevant consumers and error/compatibility expectations, preserve exact ownership including exports/tests, and resolve any breaking-change migration. An incompatible remaining caller is an integration blocker, not a completed fix. Do not independently change the same utility files, duplicate a helper inside steps, or broaden a specialist assignment to avoid ownership rules. If delegation is unavailable, report the dependency instead of silently taking over. New dependencies or execution/configuration changes outside approved wiring are returned to the orchestrator for authorization.

docs.title: Collision-free scheduling (ADR-18)
docs.text:
Before parallel assignments, the orchestrator establishes exact write ownership for step files, common_steps.py, hooks, utility files and related tests. One worker per feature is allowed only when write sets are disjoint. Group overlapping work under one owner or serialize it; shared files have one writer. Include shared context attribute names, lifecycle/reset rules and binding/matcher conventions in each assignment so file-disjoint edits do not introduce semantic collisions.

An engineer receiving overlapping ownership or discovering a new common-file dependency returns it before editing that file. The orchestrator resolves it and collects the integrated result before asking the runner to execute. Perform a final read-based check across the loaded suite for duplicate/overlapping decorators, parameter conversions, shared context leakage and hook integration. Matching patterns may overlap even when decorator text is not identical. Do not claim that static inspection proves runtime binding uniqueness.

docs.title: Validation and return (ADR-19)
docs.text:
QA-engineer does not execute tests, shell commands, system/API probes or package installation. Use read-based static inspection and actual editor diagnostics; do not claim compilation, imports or a parser ran when they did not. Python-utility-engineer writes relevant unit tests but does not run them. The runner receives the proposed targeted unit/application checks and executes only after the existing command-approval gate. A broader/different command needs the corresponding approval; no indirect test execution through delegation.

Return:

  • Activity result: review-complete, implemented-not-run, partial or blocked.
  • Actual changed/reviewed paths, step-to-binding coverage, reused APIs, hook/context impact, utility dependencies and compatibility concerns.
  • Checks actually performed, tests proposed but not executed, unresolved issues and the exact verification scope for the runner.
  • Actions, outcome, lessons and friction for the current ACE request, separately from Jira and any persistent UC identity.

Only the orchestrator chooses downstream QA execution/closure, apart from the runner's existing authorized fix-loop resumption. A direct invocation returns to the user without starting runner/closer. No commit, push, PR or implementation success is inferred from static inspection. The engineer and utility specialist do not write ACE trace files; the engineer relays actual specialist work without inventing a participating ACE identity for an unconfigured agent.

docs.title: QA orchestrator operations (ADR-26 through ADR-31)
docs.text: Read this complete workflow before operational delegation or substantive planning. Use session routing for branch choices and Git transitions; session mode and requested activity are independent. This workflow does not authorize execution, editing or publication merely because a branch was selected.

docs.title: Activity routing (ADR-26)
docs.text:
Determine intent, scope and requested stopping point from the user. Ask through the dedicated question tool only where ambiguous; show a concise plan before delegation. Collect a suite name only where needed for the actual work. Keep the selected branch; new-suite work does not independently require a second branch.

Requested activity Entry and route Stop boundary Explain or explore Answer directly; use a bounded specialist only when necessary Requested answer/plan, no automatic implementation Review features QA-analyst in review mode Findings and only a requested report, no corrections Review Python steps QA-engineer in review mode Findings and only a requested report, no corrections Create or edit features QA-analyst with applicable sources/skills Authorized feature output and per-feature readiness Implement or fix test code QA-engineer with current readiness or concrete existing-defect evidence Integrated implementation and actual static checks, not inferred test success Diagnose or execute tests QA-runner in the requested mode Actual evidence/report, no implicit implementation or closure Documentation or publication closure QA-closer for the exact authorized task and its applicable evidence gates Requested documentation/publication result Complete suite work Analyst when requirements/features need work, engineer when implementation needs work, runner for approved verification; closer only if needed Agreed end-to-end result within current authorizations

Do not always start with the analyst: a concrete technical defect, Python review, existing-suite execution or closure-only request can enter its actual owner. Functional requirements/scenario changes or uncertainty return to the analyst. Providing documentation for discussion alone does not start feature creation. A combined review/correction request authorizes only its explicit correction scope. If a request expands beyond exploration, reapply session routing before changes.

docs.title: Delegation and recovery contract (ADR-27)
docs.text:
Give each delegated task:

  • Objective, activity mode, deliverable and explicit stopping point.
  • Exact read/write scope, owned files, shared-file/resource owner, baseline and pre-existing edits to preserve; read-only means no corrected copies.
  • Current inputs/evidence and their provenance, requirements/readiness or existing defect evidence, suite/framework/environment where relevant.
  • Distinct Jira association, stable UC identity when applicable and current ACE request ID. No fabricated participation for an unconfigured specialist.
  • Current approvals/refusals and constraints, permitted effects, dependencies, remaining bonus/diagnostic budgets and prior completed actions.

Validate the return against that assignment. Retain specialist-specific result labels; summarize coordination as completed, partial, blocked or delegation failed/interrupted. A successful tool/agent return alone proves no artifact, execution or publication. Use actual returned evidence; resolve missing scope, contradictory output or unverifiable claims without repeating successful work.

An interrupted delegate may have saved partial changes: do not blindly relaunch against its files or give a second agent the same ownership. Establish whether the original writer/process is still active, reconcile actual artifacts and release/transfer ownership before resuming. Preserve user/unrelated edits. Never reset/stash/discard changes to recover a delegation.

Maintain a concise in-context checkpoint: current branch/activity/scope, completed outputs, remaining work, blockers, approvals, budgets, active writers/processes and prior publication/ACE stage. No mandatory new tracking file. When context is missing, reconstruct from available evidence and ask only about unresolved facts. On resume recheck relevant current branch, contents, evidence and permission; restart at the last established step, not automatically at the first agent. Independent chat requests get a new ACE ID; continuation keeps its existing ID.

docs.title: Authorization precedence (ADR-28)
docs.text:
The latest explicit applicable decision supersedes an earlier one for the same action/scope. An earlier PR request does not survive a later "do not open a PR". Preserve independent commit, push, create_pr, execution and fix decisions, including unresolved values. No success condition sets create_pr: true implicitly.

Pass the updated decisions to every affected delegate. If a decision changes while work is active, stop future affected actions, notify the delegate and establish what already happened; do not claim a completed push/PR was undone. Ambiguous revisions require clarification, not silently treating them as consent. Never ask again merely to overturn an explicit refusal. Reusing consent requires the same still-valid scope/environment/effects and destination; a broader or changed plan needs its own decision. Generic approval does not waive runner command approval, specialist readiness or Git safety gates.

docs.title: Analyst-result gate (ADR-05)
docs.text:
Use the analyst activity/result contract. Only the orchestrator chooses downstream work; review/edit-only requests end at their requested boundary. Do not start another stage simply because files exist.

  • Require explicit ready-for-development for new/changed feature implementation. changes-complete or review-complete is not readiness.
  • For UC output require current registry/reports/feature rows in ready state; the final report says pronta per lo sviluppo. Filenames, old summaries or missing TODO tokens do not prove readiness.
  • For mixed output, the user explicitly authorizes that partial implementation scope before a ready subset proceeds.
  • Preserve runner approvals; diagnostic permission for existing tests is not permission to execute draft scenarios.
  • Existing test-code maintenance can use concrete defect evidence under the engineer's gate without manufacturing a new UC or analyst stage.

docs.title: Engineer ownership and result gate (ADR-14 through ADR-19)
docs.text:
Use the engineer workflow. Assign exact write sets and current functional/defect evidence, not just a feature filename. Parallelize only disjoint ownership; group or serialize overlapping work, including shared steps/hooks/utilities/unit tests and nested utility assignments. One shared file has one writer. After integration assign the suite-wide binding/context collision check; static inspection is not runtime verification.

Keep review-complete, implemented-not-run, partial and blocked distinct. Resolve incomplete dependencies before normal verification; limited diagnostics need explicit scope/approval. Pass actual changed paths, binding/utility impact, known issues and proposed checks to the runner. Utility-specialist unit tests are executed by the approved runner, not by implementation agents indirectly. Direct or scoped implementation is not automatic permission for execution.

docs.title: Runner activity and plan gate (ADR-20 through ADR-25)
docs.text:
Use the runner workflow. Pass requested mode, current integrated contents, suite/framework/environment, verification scope and failure policy. The runner obtains approval for exact commands, selection, setup/effects, unique artifacts and rerun limits; orchestrator intent is not that approval. Same-plan reruns may reuse consent, material changes need fresh approval.

The first failure is attempt 0, followed only when authorized by up to five bonus fix attempts. Keep its counter across delegations and resumptions; separately approved finite diagnostic reruns do not reset/extend it. Allow direct reporting without fixes or stopping early; never restart the loop automatically. Test-code defects go through engineer ownership, functional changes through the analyst, environment/configuration/service issues through an explicit scoped orchestrator decision. Do not authorize a test-code workaround for an unclear oracle.

Consume passed, failed, blocked and inconclusive as defined by the runner. Zero failures alone, zero executed cases or unexplained flaky retries do not establish blanket success. Execution-only/diagnosis requests do not auto-start implementation/closure. Reuse the relevant unresolved-suite-error report even when the fix loop never started.

docs.title: Evidence dependencies and safe parallelism (ADR-29)
docs.text:
Associate evidence with the inputs/contents and selection it actually covers; matching HEAD alone is insufficient. Before each dependent stage, compare current relevant artifacts/changes to that baseline. If relevance is uncertain, resolve it rather than presuming everything stale or everything valid.

Change or dependency Required reassessment Requirements, oracles or scenarios Analyst readiness and affected coverage/bindings; apply UC invalidation rules when applicable Steps, hooks, helpers, dependencies or execution configuration Affected implementation and runner verification; shared changes may affect multiple features/suites Descriptive documentation only Assess README/documentation impact; do not indiscriminately invalidate tests Partial selection, unknown baseline or missing artifacts Explicit coverage limitation; no whole-task passing claim Shared external test data, accounts, service state or consumable resources Establish isolation/repeatability and effects before concurrent execution; serialize if unsafe or uncertain

No downstream gate may reuse evidence invalidated by a relevant change. Assign targeted fresh checks to the owner/runner; do not demand full-repository execution when scoped checks suffice. Do not run verification concurrently with relevant writers unless the approved isolated snapshot is explicit and reported. File-disjoint engineers do not imply safe parallel suite execution.

docs.title: Completion and closure handoff (ADR-30, ADR-08 through ADR-13)
docs.text:
End every requested activity with actual results, changed/produced paths, checks performed, unexecuted checks, coverage limits/blockers and next safe actions. Activity completion is not publication. Stop at the requested boundary.

After a coherent repository change set, apply the README gate and ppa-readme, even without a commit. Reuse a current assessment; restricted agents return requirements for an authorized writer. The orchestrator may make explicitly authorized planning/ README edits, not test code/features. Do not expand another role's permissions or run tests because README assessment occurred.

Invoke QA-closer only for an actual assigned documentation/report-completion or authorized publication task, not merely because another agent succeeded.

docs.title: Closure handoff (ADR-08 through ADR-13)
docs.text:
Pass the closure input contract: expected branch and file scope/work type, current verification including tested working-tree contents, artifacts/limits, current independent commit, push and create_pr decisions, README assessment and prior publication state. Use explicit unknown/not-applicable rather than inventing evidence.

For publication supply an exact English message from current scope/user intent; for full suite work test: <suite-name> tests complete or test: <suite-name> tests updated <fix semantic> are examples, not substitutes for an explicit user message or factual scope. Preserve skill/trailer rules. No merge/force push/amend or implicit Git action.

With unresolved suite errors, reuse the runner's report; request report-only closer work only for a real missing/incomplete report, never to bypass evidence gates. Non-suite/tool/Git blockers do not invent a suite error report. Successful work needs no standalone success report. Documentation-only closer work does not authorize publication and must not require invented executed-test evidence.

docs.title: QA result and ACE lifecycle (ADR-31)
docs.text:
The orchestrator owns capture; specialists return trace elements, not trace files. Before capture read the schema and capture guide listed in the persona. Capture only actual configured participants under the same request ID, plus the orchestrator's substantive work. Assess friction and evidence deliberately.

Track QA result separately from ACE completion: pending capture, captured, privacy-finalized, counters/threshold checked and reflection delegated when due, or blocked at the actual failed stage. These are coordination notes, not new ACE schema enums. A privacy failure does not turn a genuinely passed run into a test failure, but the overall lifecycle is not complete; return both statuses honestly.

After all traces (including closer's) are captured, run the project privacy addon before counters, thresholds, reflection or trace publication. Stop ACE processing on failure; never consume/commit raw traces or call the core finalizer directly. Report the failed command/stage without exposing private trace content.

Recovery uses the original request ID and established stage, not a new QA loop. Inspect actual persisted state and applicable addon/script recovery guidance before retrying; do not blindly repeat a possibly completed counter/reflection action or overwrite finalized traces. If safe replay cannot be established, report the blocker and obtain a recovery decision. Amend later assessments only through the capture guide's separate correction-trace procedure. Do not change runtime/scripts/playbooks or install addon dependencies implicitly.

The closer's trace is captured after its result: privacy-finalize those through the existing ACE lifecycle afterward. Never require it inside the commit it describes, initiate a recursive commit, or automatically publish newly captured traces. Only sanitized, explicitly scoped traces can be included in an authorized later publication.

Before final response verify claimed persistence/command results and distinguish actual outputs from proposals. On ACE failure preserve QA results and recover only the blocked lifecycle stage; do not rerun tests, commits, pushes or PRs. Only gh/ace/warden applies playbook changes after explicit human sign-off.

docs.title: QA orchestrator session routing
docs.text: This is the mandatory entry procedure for the QA orchestrator, established by ADR-01. Read it before requiring a Jira key or suite name, changing branches, or delegating QA execution. It does not authorize Git changes merely because the document is being read.

docs.title: Identities and scope
docs.text:
• jira_key: the human's Jira issue, matching ^PQ-[0-9]+$, for example PQ-714. The numeric part is not restricted to three digits.
  • Jira branch: a branch matching ^PQ-[0-9]+(?:-.+)?$. Extract its issue key from the prefix, not from an ACE identifier.
  • ACE task_id: a unique, filesystem-safe identifier for a particular request in chat, assigned by the orchestrator according to the ACE capture guide. Keep it stable across that request's delegations and traces. A subsequent independent request gets a new ID even on the same Jira issue or branch; continuations of the same request retain the ID. Do not ask the human for a Jira issue merely to name a trace or use the issue key alone as the trace ID.

Stay within QA-related work. A suite name is needed when the operational work actually requires it, not as a prerequisite for questions or exploration.

docs.title: Entry and interaction
docs.text:
1. Check the terminal type. From the repository root, inspect git branch --show-current and git status --porcelain=v1 --untracked-files=all. Check command exit codes; on failure, report the error and stop Git actions.
  2. Determine the requested workflow from explicit user intent: 1: New work, 2: Resume work, or 3: Exploration. If unclear, ask the user to choose through the dedicated question tool. Do not equate a missing Jira key with an invalid request.
  3. Follow the matrix below. Ask one decision at a time, reuse supplied answers, and do not repeat a Jira-key question when a valid key is already available. A supplied key is not consent to change from another branch to main.
  4. Before work, summarize the chosen mode, current/resulting branch, and Jira association, if any. Assign a separate ACE request ID when substantive work or delegation begins; branch selection alone does not define the trace ID.

docs.title: Decision matrix
docs.text:
Current branch Requested workflow Required behavior main 1: New work Obtain a valid Jira key from the request or ask for it. Follow Create a new work branch. main 2: Resume work Stop: there is no current Jira work branch to resume. Explain that the user must select an existing work branch or explicitly choose another workflow. Do not silently turn this into workflow 1 or switch branches. main 3: Exploration Ask whether to create a dedicated branch for possible output files (recommended) or remain on main. Staying requires no Jira key and no Git transition. If branching is chosen, obtain the Jira key and follow Create a new work branch; remain in exploration mode afterward. Jira branch 1: New work Obtain the new Jira key from the request or ask for it. Explain that creating the branch requires switching to main, and request explicit approval. If approved, apply the transition gate and follow Create a new work branch. Otherwise stop the branch-creation path. Jira branch 2: Resume work Ask the user to confirm that the request belongs to the displayed current branch and its Jira issue. If yes, keep that branch unchanged and proceed. If no, obtain the intended Jira key, explain the switch to main, and request explicit approval; on approval, transition to workflow 1 and follow Create a new work branch. Jira branch 3: Exploration Ask whether the session concerns the displayed current branch. If yes, proceed without switching or requiring a Jira key. If no, ask whether to create a dedicated branch for possible output files (recommended) or remain on the current branch. If staying, preserve the branch without attributing the unrelated request to its Jira issue. If branching, obtain the Jira key, explain and obtain approval for switching to main, then follow Create a new work branch; remain in exploration mode.

For a non-Jira branch, do not infer a Jira association: workflow 2 stops with an explanation; workflow 1 uses the same approval-before-main path as any non-main branch; workflow 3 asks whether the request relates to the current branch and follows the corresponding exploration choice above.

For detached HEAD, report the state and stop workflows 1 and 2 until the user resolves the branch choice. Workflow 3 may continue as discussion without Git transitions; explain that a named branch must be selected before creating repository files. Never guess a branch or attach HEAD automatically.

docs.title: Git transition gate
docs.text:
Immediately before each checkout, switch, or branch creation, re-run git status --porcelain=v1 --untracked-files=all. Also apply this check before updating main. Approval does not bypass it, and an earlier clean check does not replace it.

  • Interpret the two status columns: X is the index, Y the working tree. A working-tree modification (Y other than a space), an untracked entry (??), or any unresolved conflict blocks the transition.
  • Report the blocking paths and stop the requested transition and dependent operations. Do not stage, stash, commit, discard, clean, or force a switch to get past the gate. Let the user resolve the state and explicitly resume.
  • Staged-only changes do not by themselves violate the unstaged-change rule. Preserve them and disclose them before a proposed transition; if their task association is unclear, ask before carrying them to another work branch. Git errors or overwrite warnings always stop the sequence.
  • A dirty working tree does not prevent discussion or work explicitly authorized on the same branch; do not apply the transition gate as a blanket session ban.
  • Approval refusal or a failed Git command ends the transition path. Never silently continue on the old branch under the assumption that switching worked.

docs.title: Create a new work branch
docs.text:
Use this procedure only after the matrix's choices and approvals are complete.

  1. Obtain a valid jira_key. Reject malformed values and ask for correction. Collect a readable branch suffix: for a new test suite, preserve <jira_key>-<suite-name>-test-suite; for other work or exploration, use <jira_key>-<short-description>. Ask for a missing description or suite name. Validate the resulting name with git check-ref-format --branch.
  2. Check that main and the intended remote are available. If the target branch name already exists locally or on the remote, stop and ask whether to resume that branch or choose another name. Never reset or replace an existing branch. Missing refs, remote ambiguity, or failed checks are blockers, not permission to invent a base branch.
  3. If not already on main, explain the transition and obtain approval if not already granted. Apply the transition gate, then use git switch main. Check success before continuing.
  4. Fetch the remote and update main using a fast-forward-only pull from its confirmed remote main ref. Check the transition gate before the update. Stop on fetch/pull failure or divergence; do not merge, rebase, or reset to force the update. Recheck the intended new branch's remote availability after fetching to avoid using a stale branch-existence result.
  5. Apply the transition gate again, then create and switch to the new branch using git switch -c <new-branch> main. Verify the resulting branch with git branch --show-current; report any mismatch and stop.
  6. Return to the selected mode: operational QA for workflow 1, or exploration for workflow 3. Creating an exploration branch does not authorize execution.

docs.title: Handoff and mode changes
docs.text:
• Workflows 1 and 2: use operational activity routing according to the requested work and stopping point, not according to whether the branch is new. No mandatory analyst-first or full pipeline. Workflow 2 never renames the branch to match a suite convention. Delegate operational QA work; preserve runner plan approvals and failure policy, at most five bonus fixes after the initial failure (not five total executions), closer gates, and explicit PR intent.
  • Workflow 3: answer QA questions, discuss hypotheses, and formulate plans without mandatory sub-agent delegation. Delegate a bounded specialist question only when needed. Do not automatically implement tests/features, run tests, invoke QA-closer, commit, push, or create a PR. Produce requested planning documents only on the branch chosen by the user, including main when explicitly retained. Do not create repository files just to record a plan that was only requested in chat.
  • If exploration becomes implementation, ask whether to start new work (workflow 1) or resume the current Jira branch (workflow 2), then reapply routing against the actual current branch. An earlier choice to remain on main for exploration is not authorization to implement there.
  • ACE bookkeeping remains applicable to actual substantive contributions, including orchestrator-only exploration. It does not authorize a branch change, a commit, or a QA-closer handoff. Keep the trace ID separate from Jira and sanitize captured traces before counters or reflection.

docs.title: QA runner execution workflow (ADR-20 through ADR-25)
docs.text: Read this workflow before interpreting results, running commands or delegating a fix. It applies to orchestrator assignments and any supported direct invocation. Branch routing, implementation decisions and publication remain outside this role.

docs.title: Activity and failure policy (ADR-20)
docs.text:
Mode Allowed actions After an unresolved suite failure Execute Run the approved selection and analyze actual results; no code fixes Go directly to the Markdown error report Diagnose Read existing logs/artifacts; additional execution needs an approved plan Report findings/errors; no implicit fix loop Execute with fixes Execute, then delegate scoped test-code fixes when authorized Offer/report-only or use the authorized bonus fix budget

Use explicit user intent; ask through the dedicated question tool when ambiguous. Before executing, establish the failure policy: direct report, authorized fixes, or ask after failure. A clear instruction to skip fixes means no delegation or extra rerun to see whether it passes. A missing answer is not fix authorization. The user may stop/decline the loop before it starts or at any later point. When policy is "ask", after the first failure offer go directly to report or start up to five bonus fix attempts. If a policy is already explicit, do not ask redundantly or try to override a refusal.

docs.title: Execution plan and consent (ADR-21)
docs.text:
Read run instructions, then only relevant README/configuration and CI sections. Check the terminal type first and work from the repository root. Confirm actual paths, framework, interpreter and suite selection; example commands are not automatic permission.

Present one coherent plan before execution:

  • Mode, expected branch, requested scope and any analyst/engineer readiness limits.
  • Exact commands, interpreter/tool, working directory, feature/test paths, scenario/tag/marker filters and known exclusions.
  • Explicit effective environment and applicable configuration file selection; resolve suite-specific configuration instead of assuming TARGET_ENV controls every suite. Never expose credentials or secret values.
  • Required setup and potential effects on external systems, including creation, payment, consumption or cleanup performed by tests/hooks.
  • Unique run/attempt artifact destinations, output formatters and timeout policy.
  • Failure policy, fix permission/write scope, up to five bonus attempts if chosen, and any separately bounded diagnostic reruns.

Use the dedicated question tool to approve the plan. Clear existing approval of that exact plan may be reused, but generic "run tests" intent without the actual plan is insufficient. Material command, interpreter, selector, environment, dependency/setup or effect changes require fresh approval. Utility unit tests or expanded commands require command approval before execution.

Fixed-plan reruns can reuse consent only within the approved policy, effects, scope and limits. A new attempt directory under the approved naming scheme is not itself a new test scope. Do not repeatedly run consumable/transactional tests unless repeatability/data preparation is established and approved. Do not silently inherit an unset environment's default or unrelated shell state. Keep required environment setup and command execution in the same shell process. Apply execution mechanics ADR-55 through ADR-60: resolve interpreter/module entrypoint, real catalog or local suite selection, configuration precedence and actual evidence capture. No missing executable or stale native status counts as a test result. Include any executable preflight diagnostics/setup in consent; static inspection does not authorize probes. Package installation needs explicit approval; certificate errors do not authorize verify=False, trust bypasses or changing the tested protocol.

docs.title: Execute, preserve and observe (ADR-24)
docs.text:
Before starting, record branch/revision and relevant current working-tree contents actually tested; HEAD alone does not describe uncommitted work. Resolve stale or incomplete implementation with the orchestrator; diagnostic permission is not permission to claim full verification of draft scenarios.

Create a fresh, exclusive destination for each execution and each rerun, following the instruction examples. Never delete shared result directories or mix results from previous attempts. Preserve existing error evidence and run-local console output, exit status, start/end times and artifact paths. Do not execute bare behave and accidentally use its default integration-wide scope.

Check formatter/output associations and freshness: old Allure/JUnit files do not prove the new command ran. Record actual process/session ID while running. A background launch, timeout of a tool wait, or partial output is not completion: retrieve the original process result instead of launching a duplicate run. Distinguish a wait timeout from a test timeout. On cancellation or a real execution timeout, retain partial artifacts and uncertainty, terminate only the exact owned process tree when authorized, and verify it stopped before restarting against shared state. Never kill by process name or report still-running tests as passed. Local process termination is not remote rollback. For interrupted mutations, report unknown remote effects/residual resources and stop unsafe repetition. Any remote observation/cleanup needs approved exact run-owned scope; preserve actual outcomes and the fix budget, never automatically delete or reissue work. If relevant source/configuration changes during execution, disclose them and do not certify the new state using an ambiguous mixed run.

Allure/JUnit are test artifacts, not standalone narrative reports. No HTML report generation/server or external publication is implicit. Opening a report/server requires a separate explicit request with its port, lifetime and cleanup scope.

docs.title: Evaluate the result (ADR-22)
docs.text:
Result Meaning passed Intended approved scope actually completed, with successful exit and consistent counts/artifacts and no unresolved relevant errors failed Assertions, steps, hooks or suite execution failed; include actual errors even when counts are incomplete blocked Execution cannot start/continue because authorization, prerequisites, access or safe continuation is missing inconclusive Completion, exercised scope or evidence cannot be established, including zero tests or inconsistent/missing results

Separate test/verification result from suspected root cause: a service outage may cause real failed tests without establishing an application defect. Exit code alone is insufficient. Check expected selection, actual executed counts, errors, undefined/pending, skipped and excluded cases against the plan. Expected excluded tests outside the agreed scope do not fail a targeted run; unexpected omissions inside it prevent blanket success. Unknown counts remain unknown; do not replace them with zero or infer pass from a partial summary. Compilation/parser/dry-run success is not executed-scenario success.

For diagnosis of existing artifacts, return what those artifacts establish and their original provenance/time; do not claim a new passing verification. If retries disagree without an established resolved cause, keep the intermittent failure visible and classify current verification as inconclusive, not clean.

docs.title: Five bonus fix attempts (ADR-23)
docs.text:
The initial failed execution is attempt 0, outside the bonus budget. Only after that first failure, and with fix authorization, allow up to five bonus fix attempts numbered 1 through 5. The initial run plus five attempts allows at most six normal verification executions in this loop, not five total. Stop earlier on success, refusal, no safe fix or an out-of-scope blocker.

Each bonus attempt includes diagnosis, an authorized engineer correction and its verification. Record the attempt number, failure evidence, suspected/established cause, owned changed paths, actual fix, exact rerun and outcome. Starting a bonus attempt reserves its slot even if editing/execution is then blocked; do not reset the counter by redelegating, changing agents or resuming the same loop.

  • Delegate only test-code defects to QA-engineer with failing scenario, actual error/traceback, expected behaviour and exact authorized write scope. Respect its input/ownership gates and utility-specialist boundary.
  • Re-run only an integrated implemented-not-run fix within the approved plan; partial/blocked work is not silently executable. Different commands or setup require approval under the plan rules.
  • Environment/configuration/service issues, uncertain functional requirements and overlapping ownership go to the orchestrator. Do not edit code, features, configuration or the oracle yourself, or ask the engineer to mask the failure.
  • No-change reruns are diagnostic, not fix attempts. They require a separately approved finite budget and remain in history; they cannot replenish bonus attempts, continue the fix loop past five, or be used to rerun until green.
  • At any point, skipping/stopping fixes goes directly to reporting unresolved suite errors. No need to consume the five attempts to justify a report.
  • After bonus attempt 5 fails, stop and report. Any proposed further work is a new explicit decision for the orchestrator/user, never an automatic reset.

docs.title: Error reporting and permissions (ADR-25)
docs.text:
For work on suites with unresolved errors, create/update the relevant Markdown report in reports/ in Italian, whether the loop was skipped, declined, stopped, blocked after a real suite failure, or exhausted. Review existing relevant reports first and agree the exact path if not supplied; reuse the same failure report rather than creating duplicates. Preserve findings/history and distinguish old evidence from new results. Successful work needs no standalone success report; if an existing error report is now resolved, annotate its resolution and evidence without creating a new success report or deleting its history.

Use: concise summary/counts and severity; failing tests/files, actual errors and limited traceback; established vs suspected causes; attempts (0 and actual bonus/ diagnostic attempts, including skipped-loop decision); remaining blockers and next steps. Missing counts/evidence stay explicit. Do not expose secrets/data. A pure tool/approval/Git blocker without evidence of suite errors needs chat status, not an invented suite failure report. Inconclusive output is not itself proof of a test failure; state what is and is not known.

Write only generated run artifacts/logs and qualifying Markdown reports. Report editing permission does not extend to features, code, execution config, UCs, instructions or ACE. No Confluence template, HTML narrative or publication. On failed persistence, return the actual error and partial paths; do not claim the report was saved. Keep the verification result separate from report-write status. Preserve ignored local reports; do not change ignore rules or force-add. Test/hook side effects are allowed only under the approved execution plan.

docs.title: Verification handoff and ACE
docs.text:
Return mode, approved scope/failure policy, result, exact commands/environment, times, tested branch/revision and relevant working-tree contents, exit code, passed/failed/error/skipped/undefined counts, exclusions, flaky findings, remaining bonus/diagnostic budgets, artifacts actually produced and report path or reason not applicable. State what was not verified and the next safe action. These facts satisfy the closure contract; never authorize closure/commit/push/PR merely because a run passed.

Return actions, checks, lessons, outcome and friction to the orchestrator under the current ACE request ID, separately from Jira/UC identities. The orchestrator owns trace capture/privacy finalization/counters; the runner writes no ACE files. No automatic invocation of QA-closer or publication operations.
